ideas.hypothesis: Individual professional forecasters' inflation biases keep the same sign over time and grow with inflation variance, as asymmetric loss implies. Part of the cross-sectional disagreement therefore reflects differences in loss asymmetry rather than differences in information.

sources.role: mechanism and testable implications: asymmetric costs of over- and under-prediction produce biased forecasts and dispersion that rises with the level and variance of inflation
data and measure: SPF matched point and density forecasts, with entropy-based uncertainty and disagreement measures

ideas.test: SPF individual inflation forecasts 1981-2019. Estimate a loss-asymmetry parameter for each forecaster from their errors (GMM on forecast-error moment conditions), test whether it persists across non-overlapping sub-samples, and regress bias size on rolling inflation variance.
ideas.disconfirming: Forecaster-level biases are not persistent, or their size is unrelated to inflation variance.

ideas.hypothesis: Hybrid NKPC estimates for small transition economies that report dominant forward-looking expectations have low power against backward-looking alternatives. Simulations at Uzbekistan-sized samples will show forward-looking dominance found spuriously far more often than nominal size.

sources.role: method and finding: instrumental-variable tests of the hybrid NKPC have very low power against non-nested backward-looking models
setting: standard, open-economy and hybrid NKPC estimates for Uzbekistan

ideas.test: Monte Carlo study: simulate purely backward-looking inflation calibrated to Uzbekistan's quarterly data (about 60-80 observations), estimate the hybrid NKPC by GMM, and record how often the forward-looking coefficient appears dominant. Then re-estimate on actual data with weak-instrument-robust (Anderson-Rubin) confidence sets.
ideas.disconfirming: Power is high in the simulations, and robust confidence sets on actual data tightly exclude backward-looking dominance.

ideas.hypothesis: The Friedman-Ball effect, inflation raising inflation uncertainty, holds only in a high-inflation regime identified endogenously by a smooth transition model. In the low regime causality is absent or reversed.

sources.role: finding and setting: inflation-uncertainty causality in Turkey compared across high- and low-inflation periods split by date
method: an LSTAR model showing a joint relation between inflation level, volatility and persistence across regimes in Iran

ideas.test: Monthly CPI for Turkey and Iran 1988-2019. Fit an LSTAR-GARCH model with regime-dependent conditional variance, then run Granger-causality tests between inflation and conditional variance within the endogenously identified regimes, instead of fixed date splits.
ideas.disconfirming: Causality from inflation to uncertainty is equally strong in both regimes.

ideas.hypothesis: Announcing a numerical inflation target lowers inflation volatility more for central banks that also have an output-stabilization mandate than for those with inflation-only mandates.

sources.role: finding: in lab experiments, communicating the target reduced inflation volatility only when the central bank also cared about economic activity
method: comparing macroeconomic performance of targeting and non-targeting country groups
setting: inflation targeting in less-developed countries

ideas.test: Panel of about 60 countries 1985-2019, with dates of numerical target announcements and mandates coded from central bank laws. Difference-in-differences of rolling inflation volatility around announcements, interacted with mandate type.
ideas.disconfirming: The volatility reduction is the same across mandates, or larger under inflation-only mandates.

ideas.hypothesis: Budget deficits have a larger long-run inflation effect where the inflation-tax base (reserve money/GDP) is small, because the same seigniorage then requires higher inflation.

sources.role: mechanism and method: a nonlinear deficit-inflation link through the inflation-tax base, estimated with dynamic panel methods separating short- and long-run effects across 107 countries

ideas.test: More than 100 countries 1960-2019 (IMF IFS/WEO). Pooled mean group estimation of inflation on deficit/GDP, with an interaction between deficit and reserve money/GDP, plus split-sample estimates by financial depth.
ideas.disconfirming: The long-run deficit-inflation coefficient does not vary with the size of the inflation-tax base.

ideas.hypothesis: The inflation threshold above which inflation lowers growth is much higher in developing countries than the roughly 2 percent found for the US, and the hump-shaped relation is flatter.

sources.role: method and finding: nonparametric and semiparametric IV estimation of a hump-shaped US inflation-growth relation with a 2 percent threshold
setting: the inflation environment and targeting experience of less-developed countries

ideas.test: About 80 developing countries 1960-2019 (Penn World Table growth, IFS inflation). Estimate group-level thresholds with the same SNP-IV approach and compare them with developed-country estimates.
ideas.disconfirming: Developing-country thresholds are near 2 percent, the same as for the US.

ideas.hypothesis: Households move their inflation expectations toward realized inflation more strongly when their prior uncertainty is higher, so the updating gain rises when cross-sectional dispersion of expectations is high, as the aggregated Bayesian learning model implies.

sources.role: mechanism and method: a Bayesian learning model that explains both the mean and variance of Michigan-survey inflation expectations
measure: distinguishing disagreement from individual uncertainty

ideas.test: Michigan Survey rotating-panel microdata 1980-2019 (respondents re-interviewed after six months). Regress individual revisions on the gap between realized inflation and the prior expectation, interacted with uncertainty proxies (round-number responses, concurrent cross-sectional dispersion).
ideas.disconfirming: The updating gain is constant, or falls, as prior uncertainty rises.

ideas.hypothesis: A Kalman-filter common-factor measure of core inflation forecasts headline inflation out of sample better than exclusion-based core in economies with large food and energy weights.

sources.role: method: core inflation as an unobserved common factor across price components, estimated with the Kalman filter
setting and method: out-of-sample RMSE comparison and structural-break testing for Tunisian inflation forecasts

ideas.test: Monthly CPI components for Tunisia and about 10 other emerging economies 2000-2019. Estimate factor-based core, then compare 12-month-ahead out-of-sample headline forecasts with those from ex-food-and-energy core using RMSE and Diebold-Mariano tests, allowing for Bai-Perron breaks.
ideas.disconfirming: The factor-based core gives no significant forecast improvement over exclusion core.

ideas.hypothesis: Market-perceived inflation target bands extracted from the term structure narrow and become more symmetric as an inflation-targeting regime matures, which signals rising credibility.

sources.role: method and finding: term-structure restrictions show the market-perceived Canadian target band had the announced width but was asymmetric
mechanism: a critique of whether inflation targeting delivers credibility gains

ideas.test: Zero-coupon yields and CPI for Canada, New Zealand and the UK 1992-2019. Estimate perceived band width and asymmetry over rolling windows and regress them on regime age and on credibility events (target renewals, governor changes).
ideas.disconfirming: Perceived band width and asymmetry do not change with regime age.

ideas.hypothesis: Adopting inflation targeting lowers inflation persistence (the sum of autoregressive coefficients) because anchored expectations reduce backward-looking indexation, and the fall is larger in developing countries.

sources.role: method: comparing outcomes of targeters and non-targeters
finding: inflation targeting succeeded in lowering inflation and expectations in less-developed countries
measure: persistence estimated together with inflation level and volatility

ideas.test: Quarterly CPI for about 50 countries 1980-2019. Estimate rolling AR-sum persistence and run staggered-adoption difference-in-differences (Callaway-Sant'Anna) of persistence on targeting adoption, split by development level.
ideas.disconfirming: Persistence does not fall after adoption relative to non-targeters.
